clue.text: A new bottle of scent could be beginning to work

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might form something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: A fresh bottle of perfume might be just the thing to get you going in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' is the anagram signal for A, N and BOTTLE OF SCENT together. 'beginning to work' means the thing found at the start of a book, not getting started.
explanation.definitionFit: A book's list of chapters sits at the front, so it is literally the beginning of a written work.

clue.text: Add the dryer for free to stop competition

parts.note: to add something at no charge, 'for free', is to throw it in
a towel is what you dry yourself with

explanation.surface: A shop sweetens a deal by giving away a tumble dryer to beat its rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for free' completes 'Add': a sales extra is thrown in. 'dryer' looks like the machine but is the cloth you dry with.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from boxing, where a corner tossing in the towel concedes the fight; it means giving up.

clue.text: In essence, Lithuania is brilliant

indicators.note: In says one piece sits within the other, the country code placed inside the word for essence

parts.note: a thing's essence is its being, its fundamental nature
LT is the international code for Lithuania

explanation.surface: A patriotic claim that, at heart, the Baltic state is wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In essence' reads as the phrase 'basically', but 'In' is the containment signal. 'brilliant' is the British slang sense, not the gemstone or genius sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Belting is informal British slang for excellent, outstanding or brilliant.

clue.text: Vote for remain primarily, providing May's last thrill

parts.note: to vote for someone is to elect them

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter of remain is taken

parts.note: providing means on condition that, which is if

indicators.note: May's last means the final letter belonging to the name May

explanation.surface: A Brexit-era image: Theresa May's last days spent thrilling Remain voters.
explanation.walkthrough: Remain and May evoke the Brexit referendum and Theresa May, but they are only letter sources here.
explanation.definitionFit: To electrify an audience is to excite or thrill it, as if with a jolt of current.

clue.text: Planes of one airline take off on time

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed after the preceding piece

parts.note: to take off is to run away, flee

explanation.surface: An airline's planes depart on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take off' looks like flying but means running away; 'on' sets T after FLEE.
explanation.definitionFit: All the aircraft operated by a single carrier together form its fleet.

clue.text: Wild corgi out drinking wine

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the scrambled dog's letters surround the wine
out means put out of order, so the letters of corgi are rearranged

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: A dog gets out and goes on a wine binge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the dog's letters to ORGIC, and 'drinking' puts the wine inside. 'Wild' sits at the front looking like a description of the dog, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Orgiastic describes unrestrained revelry, so it fits wild in the sense of a riotous party.

clue.text: Initially set up, somewhat embarrassed escort recognises Tiger Woods

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means turned upwards, read from bottom to top
Initially tells us to take the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A sheepish escort spots golfer Tiger Woods after being set up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' takes S, E, E, R, T and 'set up' turns them round. 'Tiger Woods' looks like one name, but Woods is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A wood is a stand of growing timber, made up of many of these plants.

clue.text: Clear my day for hold-up in court

parts.note: to clear a sum is to net it as profit
cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!

explanation.surface: Someone cancels their plans to sit through a court case delayed by a hold-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear my day' sounds like freeing a diary; 'court' is a tennis court, not a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis the top band of the net can catch a ball and stall it, a hold-up on court.

clue.text: One who tolerates Yogi's suffering supporter?

parts.note: a yogi is one who stretches, so belonging to one who stretches
one who bears or puts up with something is a bearer

explanation.surface: Someone patient enough to put up with a yogi's pain.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'the yogi's bearer': one who bears for a stretcher. The definition is cryptic: such a person supports the injured.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretcher bearer carries a casualty on a litter, literally holding up someone who is in pain.

clue.text: In the end spouse will part to be again free

indicators.note: part means split open, so the word for living again is divided to admit the letter

parts.note: to relive is to live or be again

indicators.note: In the end means the final letter of spouse is taken

explanation.surface: A spouse ultimately leaves in order to be single and free once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will part' splits RELIVE so the E from 'spouse' goes in: RELI-E-VE.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve someone of a burden or duty is to free them from it.

clue.text: More energy consumed by kitchen implement

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed up within, so the utensil holds the letter

parts.note: a grater is a kitchen tool for shredding cheese
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A kitchen gadget that uses more power.
explanation.definitionFit: As a comparative adjective it means of larger amount or degree, the same as more.

clue.text: Where too much food goes to waste, I'm told

indicators.note: I'm told says the word is heard rather than seen, so its sound counts

parts.note: the word to be said aloud is waste, as printed

explanation.surface: A grumble that overeating means food simply goes to waste.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface implies leftovers thrown away; the definition jokes that excess food ends up round your middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Overeating adds inches around the midriff, the narrow part of the body between ribs and hips.

clue.text: Take ecstasy

definitions.meaning: to take goods somewhere is to carry or convey them
ecstasy is rapture, as in being carried away with delight

explanation.surface: An instruction to take a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ecstasy' looks like the drug but is the feeling of rapture.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means carry or convey; as a noun, being transported with joy is overwhelming rapture.

clue.text: Disregarding books after nightwear finally removed

indicators.note: after means the books piece follows the trimmed garment
finally removed means the last letter of the garment is dropped

parts.note: a negligee is a light dressing gown or nightdress
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone reads in bed after taking off their nightie, careless of propriety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally removed' drops the last E of NEGLIGEE; 'after' puts NT behind it. NT, the New Testament, is a crossword staple for 'books'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being careless means failing to pay proper attention, which is disregarding one's duty.

clue.text: Teams meeting opponents for refreshments

parts.note: football and cricket sides have eleven players, so teams are elevens
in bridge, East and South sit in rival partnerships, so E and S are opponents

explanation.surface: Teams gather with their rivals over drinks and snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge pairs North with South and East with West, so E and S face each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevenses is a British mid-morning snack and cup of tea, a light refreshment taken around eleven o'clock.

clue.text: Dutch regularly chases women, at first ignoring size

indicators.note: chases means comes after, so the picked letters of Dutch follow
at first means the opening letters of women and ignoring are taken
regularly means every other letter of Dutch is taken

explanation.surface: The setter, Dutch, admits to chasing women while caring nothing for their size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes D, T, H from Dutch, which follows W and I from 'at first'. Dutch is the setter's own pseudonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Width is a measurement across, one dimension of something's size.

clue.text: In good health, two men have celebrated

parts.note: someone in good health is well
K for king and N for knight are chess men
to own something is to have it

explanation.surface: Two healthy men have been celebrating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'celebrated' looks like the verb, but it is the adjective, famous; 'men' are chess pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrated person is famous, widely recognised by the public.

clue.text: Pleased with a replacement being nothing like beer

indicators.note: replacement says one letter of the word for pleased is swapped for another

parts.note: pleased means happy
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A drinker who is pleased with a substitute that tastes nothing like beer.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface says 'nothing like beer'; actually 'nothing' replaces the A of HAPPY and 'like beer' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ale brewed with lots of hops has a bitter, hop-flavoured taste, characteristic of beer.

clue.text: Flexible even if power were lost to Spain?

definitions.text: Flexible even if power were lost to Spain?

indicators.note: were lost to says one letter gives way and another takes its place

parts.note: flexible means stretchy, which is elastic
E is the international vehicle code for Spain
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Something stays bendy whatever happens to Spain's electricity supply.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the E of ELASTIC for P and you get the answer; or, read the clue's way, if its P were lost to E it would still mean flexible.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic as an adjective means pliable, able to be moulded or bent into shape.

clue.text: Moving flight will involve a real cost

indicators.note: involve suggests entangling or twisting, so the letters of a real cost are mixed up

explanation.surface: A warning that relocating by plane will be pricey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving flight' suggests air travel but means a flight of stairs that moves.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a staircase whose steps travel up or down, so it is literally a moving flight of stairs.

clue.text: Triumphs in offensive and matching clothing

indicators.note: in means placed inside the word for the offensive

parts.note: the Tet Offensive was a 1968 campaign in the Vietnam War
triumphs are wins

explanation.surface: Military victories, then a uniform look in clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' looks like an adjective but is a noun: the Tet Offensive of 1968.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinset is a cardigan and jumper made to match, worn together as a pair.

clue.text: Passing itinerants heading off to work

indicators.note: to work means the remaining letters are worked into a new order
heading off means the first letter of itinerants is removed

explanation.surface: Travelling workers set out for their jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes the I; 'to work' then rearranges TINERANTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something passing lasts only briefly before it goes, which is the sense of fleeting or short-lived.

clue.text: Film about English group of high-fliers

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the thin layer goes round the letter

parts.note: a film is a thin layer, a skin

explanation.surface: A movie about a band of successful English high achievers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' looks like cinema but means a thin coating; 'high-fliers' are birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A skein is the name for a flock of wild geese in flight.

clue.text: Carry on Maiden — a symbolic family feature?

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed after what precedes

parts.note: to carry is to tote
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: It reads like a title from the Carry On film series, starring a maiden.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden over in cricket is one with no runs scored, recorded as M.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an emblem, often a natural object or animal, revered as the symbol of a clan or kin group.

clue.text: Blade Runner wanting tip to secure name of foe, ultimately

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast, so the shortened runner wraps round the letter for name
wanting tip means lacking its first letter

parts.note: a ski is a runner, like the blade of a sledge

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letters of of and foe are taken

explanation.surface: It evokes the film Blade Runner, a hunter trying to pin down an enemy's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blade Runner' looks like the film title, but Blade is the definition. 'wanting tip' makes KI from SKI; 'to secure' puts N in.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade is the cutting part of a tool, and the term stands for the whole cutting implement.

clue.text: One who has seen written verses occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally means taking letters now and again, here every other one

explanation.surface: A reader who has encountered written poetry now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: An observer of an event, especially one who later testifies, is someone who saw it.

clue.text: Disturb our rest as appropriate

indicators.note: Disturb means the letters of our rest are upset into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tells others to break into our sleep as they see fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' looks like the adjective 'suitable' but is the verb 'take'. 'as' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, to pocket money, often improperly, is to put it in your pocket and keep it.

clue.text: Somehow she controls men's beastly character

indicators.note: Somehow means in some way or other, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman who manipulates men shows a brutish nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beastly character' looks like a judgement on her; it is a literal monster figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Nessie is a legendary creature said to live in a Scottish lake, so a beast of folklore.
